answer: Witness-set enrollment requires each new identity to be confirmed by a rotating panel of peers who record the confirmation on a shared ledger. Any duplicate registration surfaces as overlapping witness signatures, flagging both entries for review. An attacker must therefore recruit a fresh, non-overlapping panel for every fake identity, paying each witness a fee that exceeds the marginal value of one sybil account—an island of cost per clone. Honest users gain a calm oasis of low-friction onboarding, while the velvet glove is simply that marginal duplication never pays.
